stateMachines.previousRepresentation: Background reader, optional stdout and process return code were coordinated by scattered kill calls; several error exits never waited for the killed child.
stateMachines.authoritativeReplacement: One try/finally owner reaps the native Popen child on every exit. Once started, the reader exclusively owns and closes its stream; stopping prevents further reads.
guards: 32 MiB output cap, 30-second read deadline and one-second exit wait remain.
Native no-lazy-fetch and optional-lock flags remain.
Only the owned Popen handle is signalled; no numeric-PID kill is added.
A reader-owned descriptor is not closed by a different thread.
stateMachines.recovery: Every normal or exceptional exit stops the reader, kills an unfinished owned child and waits for it. A reap timeout fails explicitly. Ten real-child fixtures check closed pipes and actual reaping, with short fixture-only read deadlines.
stateMachines.exception: Use the standard library Popen/Thread/Event resource protocols for OS state. A parallel application state engine would duplicate their ownership model; scoped cleanup enforces the lifecycle directly.

retainedProtocolsAndRecovery.State and storage inventory:
The package owns no database tables, queue or background worker. Repository manifests,
Git trees/indexes, registered activation receipts, diagnostic baselines and release artifacts
remain the durable inputs. Consumers' databases and workflow-provider records are external
and cannot be deleted by this package.


Existing passed/findings/incomplete report variants remain authoritative. Findings require
findings; incomplete reports require issues. Empty successful rule-example wrappers and
unused artifact-URL defaults are removed. The five runtime dependencies remain: the commit
parser, Markdown parser, YAML parser, strict input validation and CLI parser all have active
production readers.
retainedProtocolsAndRecovery.Transitions and recovery:
Commands are synchronous. Invalid inputs fail before mutation. A proposed commit repair
becomes applied only after its guarded atomic write; inode, hardlink, permission and fsync
checks remain. Read-only previews never execute tests. Runtime JSON and persisted
configuration are validated at their boundaries; bootstrap programs remain dependency-free
and compatible with their system Python runtimes.

Artifact reuse requires exact source, repository ownership, current attempt, successful job,
digest and bounded safe archive contents. Missing, failed or stale evidence requires fresh
validation. Reviewed validation additionally binds the actual tree and comparison base;
it cannot substitute for exact-main artifact identity.

Release recovery inspects immutable tags and both registries before choosing a plan. It
repairs a missing publication from the same verified source and refuses contradictory
sources or bytes. A crashed upload is resolved by inspecting registry evidence, never by
assuming it failed. Existing tags and versions are never retargeted.

GitHub statuses, check conclusions, commit states and provider metadata are validated external
observations. Their fields may be independently absent when the provider has not supplied
evidence; absence cannot qualify policy. Filesystem metadata, optional source coordinates,
package/workspace metadata, catalog descriptors and rule configuration are data records,
not independently advancing workflows. Their optional facts remain optional. The legacy v6
trusted-base marker reader remains necessary while evaluating existing consumer base trees;
it never reads policy from the proposed head.

CI retains all validation, compatibility, package and documentation gates. The five workflows
own source qualification, commit policy, standards qualification, documentation publication
and release publication. Workflow-provider scheduling/retry state is external; exact-source
artifact and release checks are this package's authoritative admission decisions.
retainedProtocolsAndRecovery.Boundary exceptions:
GitHub owns its run lifecycle. `github_review_policy._completed_run` observes it with one
finite deadline; a timeout or unfinished run cannot qualify the caller. The caller still
requires a completed successful allowed workflow and rechecks the current commit status.
Artifact waiting similarly retains its explicit awaiting/verified/fresh-validation outcome.
The fixed HTTP retry schedule applies only to GET requests without a payload. Writes have
one attempt; a transport failure never proves that the external write did not happen.

The release renderer must work after only its two saved tooling files survive an older
source checkout. Its small JSON validator therefore remains self-contained; importing the
artifact bootstrap broke that recovery contract. The installed package and pre-install
artifact bootstrap validate their own JSON boundaries. Unused urllib redirect callback
arguments remain opaque; they are never consulted and the callback refuses every redirect.

The five production Python dependencies have concrete readers: ConventionalCommit parses
commit headers; markdown-it parses descriptions and templates; PyYAML validates inert
workspace/workflow documents; Pydantic validates inputs and serialized JSON; Typer owns the
installed CLI. The site uses only an ASSETS binding and owns no database, KV or R2 binding.
Markdown comment stripping retains its single typed boolean in `_strip_line_comments`:
outside and inside a comment have identical data, delimiters alone toggle the state, and
there is no persistence, external effect, retry or invalid combination to encode. Heading
nesting uses an ordered stack, with pushes and pops in `_filled_sections`; it has no
separate phase flags. Native Popen/Thread/Event protocols retain OS ownership; one scoped owner now reaps the Git child on success, failure, timeout and interruption. The bounded Git subprocess entry records the exact lifecycle and its real-child recovery tests.

publicApiMigration.analysis: RepositoryAnalysisRequest uses selection=RatchetAnalysis(baseline_path, include_warnings=...) or UnratchetedAnalysis(). The default remains strict.
publicApiMigration.valueTypes: ExecutionIssue, JSON value types and command outcomes are defined in repo_standards.core.outcome, a dependency-free module used by metadata probes.
publicApiMigration.outcomes: Match the concrete commit repair, commit-history, checkout, diagnostic-provenance and release-plan variants before reading their required data.
publicApiMigration.wireContract: CLI commands and flags retain their established interfaces. Documentation failures now correctly emit conclusion=findings; incomplete doctor receipts preserve inspection issues. Accepted review policy requires valid integer tier evidence.

qualification: Full local checks plus exact-head CI, immutable publication and deployed reference verification are required; this inventory is not qualification evidence.
